title: Festival (Jamaican Sweet Fried Cornmeal Dumplings)
summary: A soft dough of flour, cornmeal, sugar, nutmeg and milk, rolled into short cigars and deep-fried for about 2 minutes until golden. Kept warm in a low oven and served hot.
equipment: deep heavy pot or Dutch oven

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
whole milk, plus up to 30 ml more
neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Whisk the flour, cornmeal, sugar, salt, bicarbonate and nutmeg together. Stir in the milk a little at a time until the dough is soft and pliable, like modelling clay; use the extra milk only if it stays dry and crumbly.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Heat the oven to 90 °C to keep the festival warm. Cut the dough into 10 equal pieces and roll each lightly between your palms into a fat cigar about 9 cm long and 2.5 cm thick, handling it as little as possible.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Heat oil 5 cm deep to 185 °C. Fry 4-5 at a time, turning after 1 minute, for about 2 min in total, keeping the oil at about 170 °C, until deep golden. Break one open to check the centre is fluffy, not wet.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Drain on the tray and keep warm in the oven while you fry the rest. Serve hot.

tips: Overworked dough makes tough festival; mix only until it comes together.
Coconut milk instead of dairy milk gives a lovely island flavour.
If they brown before the centre cooks, lower the heat a little.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Best eaten fresh. Keep leftovers airtight for 1 day and reheat in a 180 °C oven for 5 min. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
